docs.title: tracemelt
docs.text:
Status: prototype

OTLP ingest into ClickHouse, a read-only query API and a web UI exist. There is no alert engine or SDK yet. Applies to: dev (no release exists).

tracemelt is a planned open-source, OpenTelemetry-native observability platform for metrics, events, logs and traces (MELT). It is intended to be self-hostable and licensed under Apache-2.0.

docs.title: What exists today
docs.text:
Component Status Documentation site (MkDocs Material, mike, GitHub Pages) prototype OTLP ingest (OpenTelemetry Collector to ClickHouse), token authenticated prototype, verified 2026-11-27 Query API (read-only, token guarded, gauges only for metrics) prototype, verified 2026-11-27 Web UI (overview, traces with waterfall, logs, gauge metrics, events) prototype, checked by hand 2026-11-27 Alert engine planned Node.js and Python SDKs planned Infrastructure metrics receivers planned

"Planned" means no code for it is in the repository.

docs.title: Intended design
docs.text:
The first two items are implemented in the prototype. The rest are design decisions:

  • OTLP is the only ingest contract. No proprietary telemetry protocol.
  • The OpenTelemetry Collector (contrib) receives OTLP on gRPC 4317 and HTTP 4318.
  • ClickHouse stores telemetry in tables owned by the collector's clickhouseexporter.
  • Events are structured logs tagged with tracemelt.event = "true", not a new signal.

docs.title: Query API reference
docs.text:
Status: prototype

Verified on 2026-11-27 by scripts/smoke.sh and the unit tests in api/tests. Paths and response fields may change without notice. Applies to: dev.

The query API is a read-only HTTP service over the otel_* tables. It listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 by default.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every endpoint except /api/health and POST /api/session requires Authorization: Bearer <TRACEMELT_API_TOKEN> or the session cookie described below. A missing or wrong token returns 401. The ingest token is not accepted.

This single shared token is a temporary guard. There are no users, roles or audit log yet.

TOKEN=$(grep TRACEMELT_API_TOKEN .env | cut -d= -f2)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/services"

Expected output after the smoke test has run, with your own service names:

[{"service":"smoke-1795785046-21234","spans":1,"error_spans":0}]

docs.title: Browser session
docs.text: The web UI signs in with POST /api/session and a JSON body {"token": "<TRACEMELT_API_TOKEN>"}. A correct token returns 204 and sets the cookie tracemelt_session (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, 12 hours). The cookie value is derived from the token and is not the token. DELETE /api/session clears it. GET /api/session returns {"signed_in": true} or 401.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints are GET and return a JSON array.

Path Parameters Returns /api/health none {"status":"ok"}, or 503 when ClickHouse does not answer. No token needed. /api/services since_minutes Services with span and error span counts. /api/traces since_minutes, limit, service, errors_only Recent traces, newest first. service keeps traces with at least one span from that service and still reports the whole trace. /api/traces/{trace_id} none Every span of one trace, up to 5000. 404 if unknown. /api/logs since_minutes, limit, service, q, trace_id Log records, newest first. q is a case-insensitive substring match on the body. /api/events since_minutes, limit, service, name Log records tagged tracemelt.event = "true". /api/metrics since_minutes Gauge and sum metric names. chartable is 1 for gauges only. /api/metrics/gauge name (required), since_minutes, step_seconds, service Per-service avg, min and max of a gauge per time bucket.

docs.title: Parameter limits
docs.text:
Requests outside these bounds return 422 before any query runs.

Parameter Bound since_minutes 1 to 10080 (7 days), default 60 limit 1 to 1000 service, q, name (events) at most 200 characters name (gauge) 1 to 255 characters trace_id exactly 32 lowercase hex characters step_seconds 10 to 3600, and at most 1500 buckets per request

docs.title: Query guardrails
docs.text:
The API connects as the ClickHouse user tracemelt_reader. Its limits are set in the server profile with readonly = 1, so the API process cannot raise them.

Limit Value API response when hit max_execution_time 10 seconds 504 max_memory_usage 1 GB 422 max_result_rows 10000 422 Concurrent queries for the user 16 502 Concurrent HTTP requests 32 503

The user can only SELECT from the telemetry database. The smoke test checks that it cannot insert, drop, change its settings or read system.users, and that a slow query and an oversized result are both stopped.

All SQL is fixed text with server-side bound parameters. User input is never concatenated into a statement.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Sum metrics, histograms and percentiles cannot be queried. Only gauges are charted.
  • /api/traces reports the longest span as duration_ns, which equals the trace duration only when the root span covers the whole trace.
  • q is a substring scan, not an indexed search. On large tables it will hit the 10 second limit.
  • No pagination, no caching, no CORS, no TLS.
  • Error responses carry a short reason only. Details are in docker compose logs api.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Status: prototype, ingest only

Verified on 2026-11-27 with Docker 29.5.3, Compose v5.1.4, collector contrib 0.166.0 and ClickHouse 26.8.48.11 on macOS (arm64). This covers OTLP ingest into ClickHouse, the query API and the web UI. There is no alerting or SDK yet. Applies to: dev.

This tutorial starts the single-node stack and proves that authenticated OTLP data reaches ClickHouse.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: You need Docker with Compose v2, curl, openssl and python3. Ports 4317, 4318, 8000 and 13133 must be free on loopback, or change them in .env after step 1.

docs.title: 1. Generate secrets
docs.text:
scripts/init-env.sh

Expected output:

wrote .env

The script generates an ingest token and a ClickHouse password. It refuses to overwrite an existing .env.

docs.title: 2. Start the stack
docs.text:
docker compose --profile demo up -d --build
docker compose ps --format '{{.Service}}\t{{.State}}'

Expected output, after the images have been pulled:

api running
clickhouse  running
collector   running
demo    running

The demo profile adds a sample workload: three services that send traces, logs, events and gauges. Leave the flag out to run without it.

docs.title: 3. Run the smoke test
docs.text:
scripts/smoke.sh

Expected output:

PASS  collector health (200)
PASS  logs without token rejected (401)
...
PASS  slow query killed by time limit (Code: 159)
PASS  large result killed by row limit (Code: 396)
smoke: all checks passed

There are 39 PASS lines. Any FAIL line names the check and what it got.

The test sends one span, two log records (one of them an event) and one gauge over OTLP HTTP, reads them back from ClickHouse and through the query API, and checks that the API's database user is read-only and limited.

docs.title: 4. Send your own telemetry
docs.text:
Point any OpenTelemetry SDK at the collector:

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS="Authorization=Bearer $(grep TRACEMELT_INGEST_TOKEN .env | cut -d= -f2)"

docs.title: 5. Look at it
docs.text:
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/, paste the value of TRACEMELT_API_TOKEN from .env and sign in. With the demo workload running, Overview lists storefront, inventory and payments. See Use the web UI.

The same data is available from the query API:

TOKEN=$(grep TRACEMELT_API_TOKEN .env | cut -d= -f2)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/services"

Expected output, with your own service names:

[{"service":"smoke-1795785046-21234","spans":1,"error_spans":0}]

docs.title: If something fails
docs.text: Symptom Cause and fix required variable ... is missing a value: run scripts/init-env.sh No .env. Run step 1. port is already allocated Another process holds an OTLP port. Change the TRACEMELT_*_PORT values in .env. Smoke test fails at collector health The collector is still starting or is restarting. Check docker compose logs collector. schema-init exits with an error ClickHouse was not reachable when the tables were being created. Check docker compose logs schema-init clickhouse, then run docker compose up -d again.

docs.title: Stop and clean up
docs.text:
docker compose down        # keeps data
docker compose down -v     # deletes stored telemetry and the collector queue

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
Status: prototype

No version of tracemelt has been released. Entries below describe changes to this repository. Applies to: dev.

The format follows Keep a Changelog.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Single-node Docker Compose stack: OpenTelemetry Collector contrib 0.166.0 writing to ClickHouse 26.8.48.11.
  • OTLP ingest requires a bearer token. Requests without it get HTTP 401.
  • On-disk collector export queue with bounded retries.
  • One-shot schema-init job creates the exporter's tables, so the collector can start and queue data while ClickHouse is down.
  • scripts/outage-test.sh to test durability across a ClickHouse outage.
  • Read-only query API (FastAPI) for services, traces, logs, events and gauge metrics, guarded by a bearer token.
  • Web UI served by the query API: overview, traces with a span waterfall, logs with a jump to the trace, gauge charts and events.
  • Browser sign-in: POST /api/session exchanges the API token for an HttpOnly session cookie. Strict content security policy on every response.
  • Demo workload behind docker compose --profile demo.
  • ClickHouse user tracemelt_reader: select-only, with time, memory and row limits it cannot raise.
  • scripts/init-env.sh to generate secrets and scripts/smoke.sh to verify ingest end to end.
  • Configuration reference page.
  • Apache-2.0 LICENSE and a README.
  • Roadmap and changelog pages.
  • Strict docs build as a gate before every docs deploy.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Project name in the docs is now tracemelt. The repository and docs URL remain observability-lens.
  • The landing page and quickstart describe only what is in the repository. The quickstart is now a verified ingest tutorial.
  • Quickstart moved to getting-started/quickstart.md. The old /quickstart/ URL no longer resolves.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Broken link to a missing roadmap page, which made mkdocs build --strict fail.
  • Unclosed code block in the quickstart.
  • GitHub Pages 404: Pages now serves the gh-pages branch root and the site root redirects to dev.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Status: planned

Only items marked done have code in the repository. There are no dates. Applies to: dev (no release exists).

Phases are worked in order. A phase is complete only when its acceptance checks have been run and the results recorded.

docs.title: Phase -1: truth and docs live
docs.text:
State: in progress.

Check State Docs URL returns 200 done GitHub Pages serves the gh-pages branch root done mkdocs build --strict passes done Navigation references only existing files done Every page carries a status banner done /latest/ returns 200 not done: no release exists, the site root points at dev Ports and environment variables reference done Remaining Wave 1 pages (MELT model, architecture, data model, alerting limitations, no-data troubleshooting) not done: they describe components that do not exist yet

docs.title: Phase 0: verify the quickstart
docs.text:
State: in progress. Ingest is verified: the collector accepts authenticated OTLP and writes traces, logs, events and metrics to ClickHouse, the query API reads them back, and the web UI shows them, including the trace waterfall and the jump from a log record to its trace. A demo workload exists. The alert engine does not exist yet, so alert creation and webhook delivery are unverified.

Acceptance: a new user can follow the quickstart without guessing, and every command has a recorded expected output.

docs.title: Phase 1: harden single-node
docs.text:
State: started. Done so far: secrets from the environment, token authenticated OTLP ingest, a persistent collector queue (tested with a 300 second outage and a collector restart), ClickHouse with no published ports, query guardrails on a read-only ClickHouse user, a token guard on the API.

Scope: secrets from the environment, authenticated OTLP ingest, an authenticated UI and API, a persistent collector queue, query guardrails, webhook allowlisting with SSRF protection, self-metrics, disk and retention alerts, backup and restore, PII redaction defaults, fail-open SDK defaults.

docs.title: Phase 2: production shape
docs.text:
State: planned.

Scope: Postgres for rules, state, outbox and audit; OIDC and RBAC; separate ClickHouse users; alert resolution, silences, dedup and durable notification retries; histogram averages and real percentiles; per-series alerting; a Helm chart; upgrade documentation.

docs.title: Phase 3: scale and enterprise
docs.text:
State: planned.

Scope: highly available ClickHouse, collector gateway replicas, downsampling, tiered storage, multi-tenancy, quotas, tail sampling, cardinality controls and migration guides.

docs.title: ADR 0001: Create the ClickHouse schema in a one-shot job
docs.text:
Status: prototype

Accepted on 2026-11-27. Applies to: dev.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The collector's clickhouseexporter creates its tables at startup when create_schema is true. If ClickHouse is unreachable at that moment the collector exits. A collector that restarts during a ClickHouse outage then refuses OTLP until ClickHouse returns, and senders lose data once their own retries run out. This was observed on 2026-11-27.

tracemelt must not hand-write the telemetry schema, because the exporter owns it and changes it between versions.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The long-running collector sets create_schema: false.
  • A one-shot schema-init job runs the same pinned collector binary with create_schema: true, waits until its health endpoint answers, then exits. The long-running collector starts only after the job succeeds.

The DDL is still produced by the exporter, at the same version as the collector that writes the data.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The collector starts, accepts data and queues it to disk while ClickHouse is down. Tested with a 300 second outage and a collector restart in the middle: 40 of 40 records arrived, none duplicated.
  • The schema-init image tag must be bumped together with the collector image tag. Both are pinned in docker-compose.yml and its Dockerfile.
  • A collector that starts while ClickHouse is down cannot inspect the table columns, so it leaves optional columns (currently EventName in otel_logs) empty until its next restart.
  • TRACEMELT_RETENTION is read by the job. It still only applies when tables are first created.

docs.title: Alternatives rejected
docs.text:
• Keep create_schema: true and document the gap. Leaves a data loss path open.
  • Check the exporter's DDL into the repository. Makes tracemelt the owner of a schema it does not control, and it would drift on every upgrade.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
Status: prototype

Describes the single-node Docker Compose stack as verified on 2026-11-27. Applies to: dev.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Port Service Bound to Purpose 4317 collector TRACEMELT_BIND, default 127.0.0.1 OTLP gRPC, bearer token required 4318 collector TRACEMELT_BIND, default 127.0.0.1 OTLP HTTP, bearer token required 13133 collector 127.0.0.1 only Health check, no authentication 8000 api 127.0.0.1 only Web UI and query API. Data requires the API token or a session. 8123, 9000 ClickHouse not published Reachable only on the Compose network

The stack has no TLS. Keep TRACEMELT_BIND on loopback unless a TLS terminating proxy sits in front of the collector.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
All values live in .env, written by scripts/init-env.sh. The file is ignored by git.

Variable Default Meaning TRACEMELT_INGEST_TOKEN generated Bearer token every OTLP request must carry. One shared token for all senders. TRACEMELT_CLICKHOUSE_USER tracemelt ClickHouse user, created on first start. TRACEMELT_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD generated Password for that user. TRACEMELT_CLICKHOUSE_READER_PASSWORD generated Password of the read-only ClickHouse user tracemelt_reader that the query API uses. Can be changed later; restart clickhouse and api. TRACEMELT_API_TOKEN generated Bearer token for the query API. Different from the ingest token. TRACEMELT_CLICKHOUSE_DB otel Database that holds the otel_* tables. TRACEMELT_RETENTION 72h TTL for all signals. Applied when tables are created; changing it later does not alter existing tables. TRACEMELT_BIND 127.0.0.1 Host address for the OTLP ports. TRACEMELT_OTLP_GRPC_PORT 4317 Host port for OTLP gRPC. TRACEMELT_OTLP_HTTP_PORT 4318 Host port for OTLP HTTP. TRACEMELT_COLLECTOR_HEALTH_PORT 13133 Host port for the collector health check. TRACEMELT_API_PORT 8000 Host port for the web UI and query API. TRACEMELT_COOKIE_SECURE 0 Set to 1 to mark the UI session cookie Secure. Required when the UI is served over HTTPS. Not written by init-env.sh.

The ClickHouse user and password are set only when the data volume is first created. Editing them in .env afterwards does not change the database.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
The collector's clickhouseexporter creates and owns every table. tracemelt does not define telemetry schema. The DDL runs in the one-shot schema-init job on every docker compose up, see ADR 0001.

otel_logs, otel_traces, otel_traces_trace_id_ts, otel_traces_trace_id_ts_mv, otel_metrics_gauge, otel_metrics_sum, otel_metrics_histogram, otel_metrics_exponential_histogram, otel_metrics_summary.

Events are rows in otel_logs with LogAttributes['tracemelt.event'] = 'true' and LogAttributes['event.name'] set.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Limit Value OTLP request size 4 MiB (gRPC and HTTP) Collector memory 512 MiB container limit, GOMEMLIMIT 400 MiB, memory_limiter at 80% Export queue 5000 batches, stored on disk in the collector-queue volume Export retry Up to 10 minutes per batch, then the batch is dropped

docs.title: Durability, as tested
docs.text: On 2026-11-27 scripts/outage-test.sh 300 passed: ClickHouse was stopped for 300 seconds, 20 log records were sent, the collector was restarted while ClickHouse was still down, 20 more records were sent, and all 40 were in ClickHouse 26 seconds after it came back, with no duplicates.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• A collector started during a ClickHouse outage leaves EventName empty. It cannot inspect the table columns at startup, so the optional EventName column in otel_logs stays empty until the collector is restarted with ClickHouse up. See ADR 0001.
  • Up to 5 seconds of data sits in memory. The batch processor holds data before it reaches the on-disk queue. A collector crash loses that window.
  • Outages longer than 10 minutes drop data. Retries are bounded on purpose. Nothing alerts on queue size yet.
  • One shared ingest token. No per-service credentials, no rate limits.
  • No TLS, no self-metrics pipeline, no backups, no PII redaction.

docs.title: Use the web UI
docs.text:
Status: prototype

Checked by hand in Chrome on 2026-11-27 against the demo workload. There are no automated browser tests yet. Applies to: dev.

The UI is static HTML, CSS and JavaScript served by the query API. It makes no third-party requests.

docs.title: Open it
docs.text:
1. Start the stack with the demo workload:

    docker compose --profile demo up -d --build

  2. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/.

  3. Paste the value of TRACEMELT_API_TOKEN from .env and choose Sign in.

The token is exchanged for an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict session cookie that lasts 12 hours. The token is not kept in browser storage. A wrong token shows "That token was not accepted."

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
View What it shows Overview Services with span counts and failure rate, and the latest failed traces. Select a service to see its traces. Traces Recent traces, filtered by service or failed only. Select a trace to open it. Trace A waterfall of every span, nested by parent. A failed span has a mark beside its name and a red strip under its bar. Select a span for its attributes. Log records that carry the trace id are listed below. Logs Log records, with a text search on the message and a service filter. Open trace jumps to the trace a record belongs to. Metrics Gauge metrics, charted as the average per service. Hover, or focus the chart and use the arrow keys, to read values; or switch to a table. Lines break where data is missing. Events Log records tagged as events, with their attributes.

The time range (15m, 1h, 6h, 24h) applies to every view. List views refresh every 10 seconds while the tab is visible.

docs.title: Find a failed request
docs.text:
1. On Overview, select one of the latest failed traces.
  2. In the waterfall, the bars with a red strip are the spans that failed. The deepest failed span is usually the cause.
  3. Select that span to read its status message and attributes.
  4. Read the log records under the waterfall for what each service logged.

With the demo workload, the payments service slows down and fails for 3 minutes out of every 12, so failed POST /checkout traces appear regularly.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One shared token signs everyone in. There are no users or roles.
  • The session cannot be revoked on its own. Changing TRACEMELT_API_TOKEN and restarting the API ends every session.
  • Over plain HTTP the cookie is not marked Secure. Set TRACEMELT_COOKIE_SECURE=1 when serving the UI over HTTPS.
  • No Alerts, Dashboards or Infrastructure views. Sum metrics and histograms are listed but cannot be charted.
  • Lists show the newest 100 traces or 200 records, with no paging.
  • Times are shown in the browser's time zone.
